tips.text: Malaysia frequently uses **double white** centre lines on its two-lane roads. It is the only Southeast Asian country to do so.
These **thick yellow bars** are also almost exclusive to Malaysia.
tips.note: You can very rarely see similar patterns in [Hong Kong](https://maps.app.goo.gl/PSUAhJVM8bCQUhH36) and the [United Kingdom](https://maps.app.goo.gl/BKn4346rfTwJj3L26).

tips.text:
Electricity poles in Malaysia often have **black** or **white** stickers on them.

Sometimes you will also find red-and-white or red-and-blue stripes below the black sticker.
**BERHENTI** stop signs and **BERI LALUAN** yield signs are both unique to Malaysia.
Malaysian bollards will often have the colours **black**, **white**, **grey** and **red**. Here are three examples of typical Malaysian bollards.
tips.note: There can be multiple varieties of these bollards, but the layout is mostly the same.

tips.text: This is a typical Malaysian directional sign. **Hexagonal yellow **highway shields** **are unique to Malaysia.
Malaysian kilometre markers have a unique **white-and-blue **colour scheme. Note that the hexagon shields are often visible.
In contrast to neighbouring Indonesia, **Chinese characters** are often seen in Malaysia. In fact, 24.6% of the Malaysian population is of Chinese descent.
Signposts in Malaysia almost always have **black-and-white** **stripes**.
tips.note: Within Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India, Nepal and Bangladesh. Make sure to check other clues before guessing.

tips.text: **Black-and-white **curbs are commonly found in Malaysia.
tips.note: Many other countries in Asia can also have black-and-white curbs.

tips.text: Each Malaysian state, excluding the three federal territories, has its own road numbering system with a **unique letter** at the start of the road number.
tips.note: Sabah also has A roads, but only the A2 and A7.

tips.text: **Black pole stickers** are most commonly found on the mainland.
tips.note: The black stickers on Borneo only exist in Generation 4 coverage.

tips.text: Black stickers with the text ‘**TEL TNB**’ at the bottom, are only found in Johor.
**White pole stickers** are only found on electricity poles on the island of Borneo, in Sarawak.
Lamp posts with **two small circles** on the support are mainly found on mainland Malaysia.
Lamp posts with a **triangular metal support** are mainly found on mainland Malaysia.
Electricity poles on the Borneo side typically have a **2-1 insulator configuration**, and a long **diagonal wooden support**. They are exclusive to the Sarawak region of the island.
tips.note: Indonesian poles can look similar, but they are usually not made of wood, and use smaller or no diagonal supports.

tips.text: Thin metal poles with **two parallel **pole tops are exclusive to the Sabah region of Borneo.
This lamp post with a supporting piece of sheet metal resembling a **boomerang** is found in Sarawak.
tips.note: It is more common in cities other than Kuching.

tips.text: Trash bins with a **logo resembling an ‘S’** are found in the states of Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor.
Trash bins with a **logo resembling leaves** are found in Perlis and Kedah.

Trash bins with this logo featuring a **sunny landscape**, saying **‘Alam Flora’** are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo will occasionally be absent, and it will just say ‘Alam Flora’.
**Yellow street name signs** with a black outline are specific to the state of Johor.
tips.note:
This **arrow-shaped** street sign, regardless of its colour, is exclusive to Malaysia.

Yellow signs are also found in southern [Negeri Sembilan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HG89SePzMd5WWheo6), however only the tip of the arrow will be black.

tips.text: **Green** street signs that form an arrow shape and have a **yellow hexagonal symbol **with the letters** JKR** on the left side are found in Sabah.
Assuming you are on Borneo: the state of Sabah is **very mountainous**, and much of the coverage is on mountain roads like this one.
tips.note: Sarawak generally has flatter roads. Even if you see mountains, they will usually be at a [distance](https://goo.gl/maps/5VrnWWJCBfNgREaP7).

tips.text: These **isolated rock formations**, rising abruptly from an otherwise flat landscape, can be found near the Thai border in Perlis state.
Urban areas in Labuan are dotted with **blue cylindrical containers**.
This unique **grey car** with a long front antenna can be found in Gunung Mulu National Park, Sarawak.
